Crafting and recipes

No workbench, fire or furnace is needed: every recipe is crafted from the pack. This guide explains the panel and its short crafting queue, shows how to cook on a placed stove and lists every recipe with its exact amounts.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 5 min, then look things up · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

How the Craft tab works

Open the inventory with E and choose Craft. Recipes are grouped into four sections: Timber, Fire & food, Materials and Tools & arms. Each ingredient shows as carried / required; in Survival a missing one reads 'Need … more'. The line below says 'Ready to craft', 'Gather the missing ingredients' or 'Free carry capacity for the output'. Every recipe is crafted anywhere, with no workbench, fire or furnace. Craft tab (crafting panel)

Key or actionWhat it does
Up / Down arrows, mouse wheelSelect a recipe.
Left / Right arrows, or click a sectionChange section.
Enter or C, or click QueueQueue one batch. In Creative the button reads Create and the recipe is made at once.
Shift + Enter, Shift + C, Shift + click Queue, or click Review craft allCount how many batches you can make now, at most 256. The button then reads 'Confirm all: … batches'. Press again, or click it, to queue them all as one order. If your pack changes first, you get a new count instead.
Cancel or Stop queueCancel drops the review. Stop queue appears while orders wait and clears them all. Nothing unfinished is spent.
Ready recipes buttonShow only recipes you can make now, including room in the pack for the result. Click again to show all.
Star buttonStar or unstar the selected recipe. You can star up to four.
Starred recipes button, or a starred recipe's nameList your starred recipes from every section, or jump straight to one.
  • Ready recipes, Star and Starred recipes are the three small icon buttons under the section buttons. Hover one to see its name. Ready recipes and Starred recipes are highlighted while switched on. Ready recipes filter (Craft tab)
  • Each starred recipe also gets a button with its name under the icons. A fifth star is refused with 'Four favorites pinned; unstar one to make room'. Choosing a section leaves the starred list. Starred recipes (Craft tab)
  • The Ready filter works on the starred list too. If nothing matches, the list says 'No recipes match these filters'.
  • Stars and the Ready filter last for this session only. They are not saved with the world.

The crafting queue

  • In Survival every craft is an order in a short queue. Queue says 'Queued … | materials kept until finished'. Each order takes 0.8 seconds, then the next one starts. Survival crafting queue
  • The panel, and the screen during play, show 'Crafting (…) | recipe' with a progress bar. The number counts the orders in the queue, including the one being made.
  • Up to 8 orders fit. A ninth is refused with 'Craft queue full (8 orders) | finish or cancel in Craft'. A Confirm all order counts as one: all its batches finish together after 0.8 seconds.
  • Materials stay in your pack until an order finishes. If you cannot afford an order when you ask, nothing is queued and the status line says 'Cannot queue … | check materials and carry capacity'.
  • Queued orders do not set materials aside. If an earlier order or anything else uses them, or the result no longer fits, the order shows 'Waiting' and the status line says 'Craft waiting | restore materials or pack space, or cancel in Craft'. Nothing is spent until the whole order can finish.
  • Crafting carries on whether the inventory is open or closed. It stops while the pause menu, the settings or the fullscreen map is open, and continues afterwards.
  • Stop queue clears every order and says 'Craft queue cancelled | all unspent materials kept'.
  • Queued orders are not saved. After you reload the world the queue is empty and the unspent materials are still in your pack. Switching to Creative also empties the queue.
  • In Creative there is no queue. The ingredients are free, but the result still needs room in the pack ('Not enough free carry capacity').
  • A crafted tool is equipped at once and a crafted boat is selected.
  • You cannot open the inventory while inside a vehicle.

Crafting on a server

  • Crafting works only in Survival ('Crafting on servers requires Survival mode').
  • Each order still takes 0.8 seconds. Then the status line says 'Requesting … | awaiting server', and the next order waits for the server's answer.
  • A refusal reads 'Crafting refused: … | materials kept'. Stop queue cannot recall an order that was already sent: 'Queued crafts cancelled | submitted craft still awaits server'.
  • While crafts are queued, chests, Home storage and furniture storage wait for them, for example 'Chest waiting for the current server action | items kept'.
Good to know. Counts are half-metre pieces. One full one-metre block is 8 pieces, so a recipe that needs 8 of a material needs one block of it.

Which ingredients can be mixed

A few ingredients accept a whole group of materials, and you can mix the members freely. Interchangeable ingredients

  • Boards: any of the 15 board species, mixed freely. Doors by wood are the exception: they need boards of exactly their wood.
  • Natural stone: any of 26 natural stones.
  • Plant fiber or Wool.

Every log has its own splitting recipe, so there is no shared hardwood group. Each makes boards of its own species; Deadwood makes Alder boards.

Every other ingredient must be that exact material: Sand (not other sands), Clay (not ochre, umber, sienna, cracked or banded clay), Reeds (not Tall reeds), Limestone, Granite, Cobblestone, Moss, Chalk, Basalt, Red rock, Marble, White plaster, Wildflowers, Paper screen, Glass, Charcoal, Feather, Raw meat, Venison and TNT.

Good to know. Not usable as natural stone: Magma stone, Iron ore, Bog iron, Amethyst, Salt, Sulfur crust, Mineral crust, Geyser stone and any crafted masonry. Sandstone is the exception: it counts as natural stone, although you can also craft it from sand.

Quick craft with X

Select a recipe on the Craft tab first. Then, with the inventory closed, each press of X queues one more batch of that recipe in the same 0.8-second queue. It works on foot in Survival. Quick craft (X)

  • If the selected recipe lacks materials, nothing is queued and the status line says 'Missing materials for … | pick another recipe on the Craft tab'. X never switches to a different recipe.
  • In Creative, X only says 'Crafting uses carried resources in survival'.
  • X does nothing while you are in a vehicle. Its key binding is called Craft selected recipe in Settings > Controls > Key bindings.

Fire, glass and cooking

Fire work is Craft-tab crafting, not a placed furnace: burn 4 boards into 2 Charcoal, then spend Charcoal to cook meat, fire Sand into Glass, blow Glass into flasks, and fire clay, limestone and lacquer. Fill flasks by pressing T at water. You can also cook meat on a placed cooking stove (next section). Charcoal, cooking and glass (no furnace)

Tip. Besides the 'Fire glass' recipe, the Survey workshop landmark's one-time find gives 8 Glass.

Cooking on a stove

A placed Cooking stove cooks Raw meat or Venison with Charcoal. It uses the same two recipes as the Craft tab: one Raw meat and one Charcoal make one Cooked meat, and one Venison and one Charcoal make two. Each batch takes 0.8 seconds. Cooking stove

  1. Open E > Build and click the Stove plan. In Survival the Build tab appears only while you carry a Furniture hammer; in Creative it is always there.
  2. Choose Feet (a board wood) and Body (Stone or Iron). In Survival, placing the stove spends one board of that wood and six Stone or six Iron ore pieces. Creative placement is free.
  3. Aim at the top of solid ground, press R to turn the ghost and right-click to place it. The stove is one metre square and one metre high.
  4. Press B to put the plan away and select an ordinary block or empty hands. Then right-click the stove from within 6 m. The inventory opens on its Cooking stove tab.
Key or actionWhat it does
Add raw meat, Add venison, Add charcoalMove one from your pack into the stove. Shift + click moves as many as fit.
Start one batchCook one raw piece. That piece and one Charcoal stay reserved until the batch finishes.
Cancel | keep ingredientsStop the batch. Nothing is spent; the food and Charcoal stay in the stove.
Take cooked meatMove finished Cooked meat into your pack. It needs free pack capacity.
Take raw, Take charcoalMove food or Charcoal that is not reserved back into your pack.
  • The stove holds up to 16 raw pieces, 16 Charcoal and 32 Cooked meat. It takes one kind of raw food at a time: take out the meat before adding venison, or the other way round.
  • Start cooks one batch only. Press it again for the next one; the stove never starts another batch by itself.
  • Start can refuse with 'Add raw food before cooking', 'Add charcoal before cooking' or 'Take out cooked food to make room for the complete recipe'.
  • Creative uses real carried food and Charcoal too. The stove never makes free Cooked meat.
  • A batch keeps cooking while the panel is closed or you walk away. It stops while the pause menu, the settings or the fullscreen map is open, or while you are dead, and continues afterwards.
  • Saving keeps the contents and the time left. Nothing cooks while the world is closed.
  • Moving or turning the stove keeps its contents. Empty it completely before taking it up, or you see 'Empty the cooking stove before removing it'. Furniture controls are in Building basics.
Good to know. The stove only cooks meat. It has no flame, gives off no heat, does not hurt you and does not set nearby wood alight. It is not a furnace and cannot smelt or fire glass, bricks or plaster.

Cooking on a server

Cooking also works when you join a server or LAN world and when you host your own world. Right-click the stove as usual. The tab first says it is waiting for the server, and after each click the buttons wait until the server confirms your pack. If the stove hint says 'Cooking waits for the server world, stock and recovery state', wait a moment and try again. Other players can use the same stove, plot claims still apply, and the server keeps cooking a started batch after you leave.

Careful. Cooking on a stove does not count for the Hot meal milestone. In Survival, craft Cook raw meat or Roast venison once on the Craft tab to reach it.

Gathering and reading the pack

Cutting a log on a natural tree, or a cactus stem, brings down that piece and everything growing from it. Cut the bottom log to take the whole tree. Cut a branch and the trunk below it stays standing. Felling trees

  • In survival the chop takes as long as all the wood and leaves it removes together. All of it goes into your pack.
  • If the whole harvest does not fit, the status line says 'Need X capacity free to collect this connected tree' and nothing is cut.
  • A log you placed yourself breaks like any other block, one piece at a time.
  • A finished tree reports 'Felled a tree' with the number of logs and leaves.

Shores mix Clay (below sea level), Gravel and Sand. Desert ground is Sand. Reeds grow in wetlands. Wild flax grows in some meadows of worlds made with the current generator. Feathers, wool and meat come from animals. Where crafting materials come from

Good to know. Older worlds have no Wild flax, so use Wool for bindings there.

Open E > Pack to see what you carry as a grid of icons. Tools come first, then food and drink, blocks, materials and spawn eggs, each group sorted by name; the sort button switches to one alphabetical list. Ctrl+F searches by name. Pack tab: Items and Character

Key or actionWhat it does
Left click an itemUse it, select it or equip it. A material with no use says it is stored as a crafting resource.
Hover an item, then press 1-9 or 0Bind it to that hotbar slot.
Drag an item onto a hotbar slotBind it to that slot while the inventory is open.
Mouse wheel, or the Previous / Next buttonsPage through the items.
Pack / Character iconsSwitch between the item grid and a turning character portrait.

Hover an item for its name, amount, category, a short description and click hints; in Pack the tooltip also says how to get it and how much capacity one piece takes. The side panel shows the item, its short description and what it is used for. Item tooltips and 3D previews

Good to know. 'USED IN' shows only the first recipe that names the exact item. Some stones count through the natural-stone group, so their panel can say 'USE: PLACE / BUILD' even when a recipe accepts them.

Block types and water kinds

At Voxelgame dfeb362d the Blocks reference lists 285 block types besides Air. Each has its own name and colour. Recipes on this page name the blocks they use. Block types and material families

  • Six block types are water: Water, Hot spring water, Dark fjord water, Fresh water, Black water and Boiling water.
  • Iron ore and Bog iron can be mined and placed. No Craft-tab recipe uses them, and the game has no smelting yet. Iron ore can pay for the iron body of furniture such as the cooking stove.
  • Glow crystal is a glowing decorative block. No recipe uses it, and the world does not generate it naturally. The Stone overlook landmark usually has one piece.

All 151 recipes

Every recipe in this version, in the order the Craft tab shows them. Each makes the stated amount from the stated inputs in one craft. The 90 doors by wood come last in the Timber section, after the Small sailing boat, and have their own table here.

When a door recipe is selected, its Style, Wood and Size buttons jump to another door recipe. Style cycles Plain, Panelled and Windowed; Wood cycles the 15 woods and, for a plain door, Any boards; Size switches between 1 x 2 m and 2 x 3 m. Choose a wood before changing the style of an Any boards door.

Lanterns, rifles and explosives

Red lantern, Alder rifle, Four rifle rounds, TNT and Two dynamite sticks use only materials you can gather or craft: stone, sand, reeds, boards, Paper screen and Charcoal. No recipe uses Glow crystal. Glow-crystal recipes in survival

Planned, not in the game. A placeable furnace or campfire, smelting, metal tools and tool durability are planned and not in this version. The cooking stove only cooks meat.

How this guide was checked
